fault_notes: The agent responds impatiently and condescendingly when Emily explains that she has contacted S-Net several times about the same unresolved broadband fault. The agent dismisses her frustration and implies she should already understand the troubleshooting process, creating a clear rapport failure despite continuing with basic checks. [On saving, two unlisted faults added: empathy (the customer reaches -51 and the agent never acknowledges the feeling once; 'There's no need to get worked up' is the opposite of empathy); noconfirm (the fault is left unresolved and the agent never checks it is fixed).]

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net. You're speaking with Mark. How can I help you?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Mark, I'm Emily Carter. I'm calling again about my broadband. This is probably my fourth call now, and the connection keeps dropping several times a day.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right. I'll need to locate the account first. What's the phone number registered with S-Net?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And for security, can you confirm the first line of your registered address and your account PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's 42 Willow Close, and my PIN is 6392.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, verified. So, what exactly is wrong with the broadband?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It disconnects randomly. The router light turns orange, then eventually it comes back by itself. I've already explained all this on my previous calls.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Well, I'm the person speaking to you now, so you'll need to tell me the details. I can't just guess what happened on another call.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I understand that, but shouldn't there be notes on the account? I've had an engineer appointment and two troubleshooting calls already.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'll look at the notes. Give me a moment. There are a few entries here, but I still need to go through the standard checks.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's fine. I just don't want to spend another half an hour doing the exact same things if they've already been done.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Everyone has to go through the process, Emily. Being impatient about it won't make the checks any quicker.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'm not trying to be impatient. I've been dealing with this for over a week, and I work from home. It's affecting my meetings.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can't change the process just because it's inconvenient. Let's establish whether the router is connected properly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The cables are connected properly. The previous adviser checked them with me, and the engineer checked the socket.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, but I'm asking you now, so please check them again rather than assuming everything is fine.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I've checked them. Everything is firmly connected. The broadband still drops even when nobody touches the router.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Fine. Is the router plugged directly into a wall socket, or are you using an extension lead?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's plugged directly into the wall. That's how the engineer left it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: All right. Have you tried restarting the router?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, several times. I've switched it off for a few minutes and turned it back on, just like the last adviser asked me to do.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And yet you're calling again, aren't you? Clearly, restarting it hasn't fixed it, so we'll have to do something else.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Exactly. That's why I'm calling. I need someone to investigate the fault instead of asking me to restart the router again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: There's no need to get worked up. I'm trying to help, but I need you to cooperate with the checks.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am cooperating. I'm answering everything you're asking. It's frustrating when it feels like nobody has read the previous case notes.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'll check the connection history. Don't worry about the earlier calls for now. We need to work through what I can see today.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay. The connection usually drops in the afternoon and sometimes late at night. It doesn't seem to follow a clear pattern.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm looking at the line history now. There are some disconnections recorded. What colour is the broadband light when it happens?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It turns orange, then flashes for a while before the connection comes back.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That usually means the router is losing its connection to the service. It doesn't automatically mean there's a fault with our network.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I know, but the engineer tested the internal wiring and said it looked fine. He mentioned the line might need further investigation.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Well, engineers sometimes say things like that without finding a definite problem. Did you receive a report from the visit?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I received a text saying the visit was completed. I wasn't given a detailed report.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right. I'll run a remote line test. It may take a minute, so please stay on the line.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure. I hope this gives us something more useful than another restart.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The test is complete. I'm seeing intermittent instability, but the line is responding at the moment.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That sounds like the problem I've been reporting. Can you tell whether it's something that needs an engineer to look at?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The test doesn't give me enough to book another visit immediately. We may need to monitor it before deciding what to do.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: But we've been monitoring it for a week already. I've called repeatedly and had a visit. What more needs to happen?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm not sure what you expect me to do if the line is working during the test. I can't manufacture a fault when it isn't showing one.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'm not asking you to manufacture anything. I'm telling you it repeatedly disconnects, and the system has recorded instability as well.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: All right. I'll check the previous case notes again and see whether there's anything we can use to move this forward.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you. The previous reference number is 583741, if that helps.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I've found that case. It says the router was restarted and the engineer checked the connection at the property.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly. The fault continued after that, which is why I contacted support again yesterday and today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The notes don't show a confirmed external line fault. That means I can't simply assume the same issue is still present.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I understand you need evidence, but the connection keeps failing. Could you add the new test results to the existing case and escalate it?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can add a note about today's test. Escalation usually requires the standard process to be completed first.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What standard process is left? We've restarted the router, checked the cables, had an engineer, and now you've run a line test.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: There may be additional monitoring steps, depending on the case. I'm adding the result and the recurring disconnections to the notes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Please make sure you mention that it's affecting my work. I've had to reconnect to meetings using my mobile hotspot, and that's costing me data.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I've included that in the notes. You can also use the S-Net app to report a new disconnection when it happens.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I've already reported them through the app. I can keep doing that, but it feels like I'm collecting evidence for a problem that should have been resolved by now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can't promise a resolution today. The line is currently responding, and I've documented the instability and your previous contact history.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'm not expecting you to promise something you can't control. I just need a clear next step and some indication that this is going somewhere.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: For now, keep the router connected and report any further disconnections with their approximate times. That will give us more information if the issue recurs.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It will recur. It has happened every day this week. I'll record the times again, but I don't see why the previous records aren't enough.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The records help, but additional examples can make the pattern clearer. I've saved today's findings against the existing case reference.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: All right. Please make sure the case doesn't get closed just because the connection happens to be working while we're on the phone.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I've added a note that the intermittent fault remains unresolved from your perspective. The case record will show the checks completed today.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you. I just hope I don't have to explain everything from scratch if I call again tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The case notes are saved, so another adviser should be able to see the history. Is there anything else you'd like help with today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that's everything. I hope the next step happens soon because this is becoming exhausting.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: All right, Emily. Keep the router connected and note any further interruptions. Thank you for choosing S-Net, and have a good day.
